scenario: Module-level __getattr__ (PEP 562) synthesizes the attribute at access time, with no bare-name binding anywhere in the module that could mask the MODULE_ATTRIBUTE bug behind the unrelated load-outside-call-position check.
human_note: Same scenario as fixture 16 (pkg/lazy.py has no attribute named vulnerable written anywhere, only a __getattr__ that synthesizes it), but lazy.py fetches the real function via importlib.import_module(...) + getattr(module, "vulnerable") -- the name 'vulnerable' appears only as a string literal, never as a bare ast.Name/Attribute Load. Fixture 16 had a coincidental `return target_func`-shaped bare-name binding that let D3's _LoadOutsideCallCollector mask the MODULE_ATTRIBUTE bug this scenario exists to catch, independent of whether the D5 fix is present. This variant removes that coincidence: the MODULE_ATTRIBUTE existence check (D5) is the only route to a correct (non-not_reachable) verdict here.
